subtype: Screams as alarm and help calls [Interpreting]
passage: I'm Manoj, and I used to think a scream was a joke. Siddharth and I would shriek across the field to scare each other, and everyone laughed. So when someone screamed near the back gate one evening, I rolled my eyes and kept kicking the ball. Siddharth stopped. "That didn't sound like a joke." We went to look, carefully, from the corner, and saw a younger boy on the ground, holding his knee. Siddharth ran to get the caretaker while I stayed with him. Since then I never use a scream as a prank, and I never ignore one.

qa.q: Where did someone scream one evening?
qa.a: Someone screamed near the back gate.

qa.q: What was Manoj feeling when Manoj first heard the scream, and what changed?
qa.a: Manoj assumed it was a joke and eye-rolled. After Siddharth said it didn't sound like one, Manoj felt worried enough to go and look.

qa.q: What should someone do when they hear a scream that might be a prank?
qa.a: Take it seriously, check safely and call for help. Ignoring it could leave someone hurt.

qa.q: How might the younger boy on the ground have felt?
qa.a: He was probably scared and in pain, and relieved when someone came. If everyone ignored screams, he would have had to wait.

grounding: A teenager learns to take a scream seriously even when it might be a prank, checking safely and calling for help.

subtype: Screams as alarm and help calls [Interpreting]
passage: Note from Ms. Irawati, science teacher. This afternoon Asif heard a scream from the lab corridor. Some students near him grinned and said it was probably a prank, as there had been one last week. Asif hesitated for a second, then said, "What if it's real?" He walked toward the sound, looked around the corner from a safe distance and saw a girl on the floor beside a spilled tray. He came straight to me. We reached her together, and I called the nurse. I thanked Asif for taking it seriously. I have also reminded the class why a false scream is unfair to everyone.

qa.q: Where did Asif hear the scream?
qa.a: He heard it from the lab corridor.

qa.q: What was Asif thinking when he hesitated and said, "What if it's real?"
qa.a: He was unsure if it was a prank but worried someone might really need help. His choice to check shows he put safety first.

qa.q: What went well in how Asif handled it?
qa.a: He checked from a safe distance and fetched an adult rather than ignoring it. That is better than assuming a prank.

qa.q: How might the girl on the floor have felt when help came?
qa.a: She was likely frightened and relieved to be found. If the scream had been ignored as a prank, she would have waited longer.

grounding: A teenager takes a scream seriously despite the chance of a prank, checks safely and calls for help.

subtype: Screams as alarm and help calls [Interpreting]
passage:
Wednesday
This evening I heard a scream from the stairwell of our building. A long one, then "Help!" My first thought was, it's Darshan again. He's always pranking, hiding and yelling to make us jump.
But it didn't stop. So I went down carefully and looked over the rail. Darshan was at the bottom of the stairs, holding his ankle, face white.
I shouted for Mr Pillai on the ground floor, who came running and called Darshan's mother. They took him to the clinic. It's a bad sprain.
Later Darshan texted: "Thanks for checking. I know you thought it was fake."
I did. I'm glad I checked anyway.
And he said he's never doing fake screams again.
- Kishore

qa.q: Where was Darshan when Kishore looked over the rail?
qa.a: At the bottom of the stairs.

qa.q: What was Kishore thinking when the scream first came?
qa.a: Kishore felt doubtful and a little annoyed, suspecting another of Darshan's pranks.

qa.q: What did Kishore do that was right?
qa.a: Kishore checked carefully and shouted for an adult, Mr Pillai, instead of ignoring the scream.

qa.q: How might Darshan see his past pranks now?
qa.a: Darshan probably regrets them, realising fake screams made it harder for people to trust his real call for help.

grounding: A teenager's diary shows taking a scream for help seriously even though the friend often pranks, and calling an adult.

subtype: Screams as alarm and help calls [Interpreting]
passage:
Near the village canal, Madhuri heard Lokesh yelling, "Help! Help me!"
The other kids laughed. "He's faking again. Last week he pretended a snake bit him."
But this yell sounded different: high, panicky. Madhuri ran to the bank, staying on the firm path. Lokesh was knee-deep in the mud near the edge, one foot stuck, grabbing at reeds.
"Don't pull too hard!" she called. "Stay still!"
She shouted to the men working in the nearby field. Two of them came running with a long bamboo pole. Lokesh grabbed it, and they pulled him out, his chappal lost in the mud.
Later, still shaking, Lokesh told Madhuri, "Nobody believed me because of my jokes. I'll never fake it again."

qa.q: What did the men bring to pull Lokesh out?
qa.a: A long bamboo pole.

qa.q: What was Lokesh feeling when stuck in the mud?
qa.a: Lokesh felt panicky and frightened, stuck and unsure if anyone would believe his yells.

qa.q: What did Madhuri do that was safe and wise?
qa.a: Madhuri checked from the firm path without going into the mud and called the adults in the field for help.

qa.q: How did the other children see Lokesh's yells?
qa.a: They thought he was faking again, because of his earlier pranks.

grounding: In a village, a teenager takes a scream for help seriously despite past pranks, checks safely and calls adults.

subtype: Screams as alarm and help calls [Interpreting]
passage: On a windy evening by the river in Lisbon, Kofi and Ines were walking back from football when a scream came from under the bridge: "Help! Somebody!" Ines rolled her eyes. "It's those Year 10 boys again. They did exactly this last week and laughed at everyone who ran." Kofi hesitated. The voice sounded higher and thinner this time. "If it's a prank, we look silly. If it isn't..." They didn't go under the bridge alone. They waved over a couple walking a dog and went together to the railing, where they could see down. A younger girl was sitting on the wet steps holding her ankle, her scooter on its side. Kofi called the emergency number while Ines stayed with the girl, and the couple fetched her parents from the café. Later Ines said quietly, "Those prank screams nearly made me walk past."

qa.q: Where did the scream come from?
qa.a: From under the bridge.

qa.q: What was Kofi feeling when he hesitated?
qa.a: Kofi felt torn and uneasy: worried about looking silly if it was a prank, but more worried someone was really hurt.

qa.q: How did Kofi and Ines check safely?
qa.a: They didn't go under the bridge alone; they brought the couple with the dog, looked down from the railing, then called for help and fetched the girl's parents.

qa.q: How had the earlier prank affected Ines?
qa.a: The Year 10 boys' fake screams made Ines doubt a real one, and she admitted it nearly made her walk past.

grounding: It shows teenagers taking a scream for help seriously despite past pranks, checking safely and calling for help, and how false alarms erode trust.
